why: The runtimes coai-mcp runs on a NATIVE Linux host (a Linux kernel that is not WSL), and for each the first coai-mcp release that does (E2 of research/PLAN_kimi_and_vibe_on_native_linux_E2.md, DN1).

ONE file, read by BOTH sides: the server embeds it (CoaiMcp.Runners.native-linux-admission.json; HostAdmission.MeasuredOnNativeLinux IS its runtime names) and the extension's ON_NATIVE_LINUX_SINCE in src/runtimeSince.ts is held to it by its own test (nothing parses the other side's source).

A runtime with NO entry is REFUSED on a native Linux host: an absent fact refuses. An entry is added by an edit to THIS file in the change that carries the measurement; `source` names the RESULTS section whose cells are the evidence,

and the runtime must also hold a confined, measured `linux` row in shared/consultant-limitations.json (a test holds that). `since` is the next minor after the newest released src_mcp when the entry was made; whoever cuts the release keeps it level with the tag (DL14).
Kimi has no entry until E3 measures it.
